def find_inv(s, minlen=12, maxgap=200):
    hits=[]

    for i in range(len(s)-minlen+1):
        a=s[i:i+minlen]

## Report on `region.fasta` (`>region_002`, 3,000 bp)

**Overall composition:** 3,000 bp, 43.6% G+C (A 887, T 804, G 661, C 648). The region is not uniform — it splits into GC-rich coding stretches and AT-rich intergenic stretches.

### 1. Two large, complete protein-coding ORFs (converging)
| Feature | Strand | Coordinates (1-based) | Size | GC | 3rd-codon GC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ORF1 | **+** | **35–703** (ATG 35–37; stop TAA 700–702) | 669 bp / 222 aa | 48.6% | 58.3% |
| ORF2 | **−** | **2076–2747** (on reverse complement) | 672 bp / 223 aa | 51.6% | 54.9% |

Both have a valid start and stop, elevated GC and strongly elevated third-position GC (typical of real coding DNA), whereas the intergenic stretches are markedly AT-rich (28–33% GC). The two genes are transcribed *toward each other* (convergent), with ~1.37 kb separating their 3′ ends.

**Shared motif:** both predicted proteins contain a `V(I)ITGGG` glycine-rich motif at nearly the same relative position (ORF1 ~Ser107, ORF2 ~Val114), suggesting the two products belong to the same enzyme family — i.e., they may be a paralogous pair. (No homolog database is available here, so the exact family can't be assigned from sequence alone.)

Translated ORF1 (222 aa):
`MWTVSWLRDMLGESLIQDARAQDLSPEDLLNKKASCVPPGCNGLMTVLDWLTNPWEPYKRGIMIGFDSSMDYAWIYRSILESVALTLKNNYDNMCNEMNHFAKHVIITGGGSNSDLFMQIFADVFNLPARRNAINGCASLGAAINTAVGLGLYPDYATAVDNMVRVKDIFIPIESNAKRYDAMNKGIFKDLTKHTDVILKKSYEVMHGELGNVDSIQSWSNA`

### 2. A striking tandem-repeat array (the most notable feature)
A ~427 bp repetitive segment lies between the two genes:

- **Coordinates 1343–1769: seven tandem copies of a 61-bp unit** (61-bp periodicity confirmed by sequence self-comparison; copies start at 1343, 1404, 1465, 1526, 1587, 1648, 1709).
- Each unit has a **conserved 5′ head ≈ `GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAACA`** (~28 bp) followed by a variable ~33-bp tail. Consensus 61-mer: `GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAACAC GAGATACCGGACTGCGTAGTCCCGTATCTCTTC`. The conserved core `CCCCGCTGGCGCG` occurs 7× (at 1350, 1411, 1472, 1533, 1594, 1655, 1716).
- This array is itself GC-rich (56.4%) — higher than the surrounding intergenic DNA.

**Truncated/degenerate relatives upstream** of the array, in the 704–1342 intergenic zone, at ~**754, 811 and 860** (e.g., `GGTTTATCCCCGCTGATGCAGGGAACA…`), so the repeated element is a small dispersed family of ~10 copies across 754–1769, with a clean tandem block only in the middle.

### 3. Other observations
- No significant inverted repeats / stem-loops (no IS-type terminal inverted repeats, no hairpin-forming CRISPR-like palindrome), and the repeat unit is not palindromic — so this is not a classic insertion sequence or a CRISPR array.
- Longest homopolymer is a 7-nt A-run (`AAAAAAA`), i.e., nothing unusual.
- Overall layout: `[AT-rich 5′ ~34 bp] – ORF1(+) 35–703 – AT-rich intergenic 704–1342 (with degenerate repeats) – 61-bp tandem array 1343–1769 – AT-rich intergenic 1770–2074 – ORF2(−) 2076–2747 – AT-rich 3′ tail 2748–3000`.

### Summary
The sequence is not anonymous: it carries **two complete, GC-rich, oppositely-oriented genes (~222–223 aa) that share a `V(I)ITGGG` motif and are therefore probably related**, separated by AT-rich spacer that contains a **prominent 61-bp tandem-repeat array (~1343–1769, seven copies) plus three degenerate copies near 754–860**. The high GC of the genes versus the very AT-rich, repeat-bearing spacers is the other notable feature. Everything above is annotated with the coordinates given.
